text: A data breach is an incident where protected data is accessed, disclosed, altered, or destroyed without authorization. Organizations that handle breaches well follow roughly the same five-stage lifecycle, and this lesson closes out Chapter Five with it.

Detect, something triggers the alarm, a monitoring alert, an unusual pattern in the audit log. Contain, stop the ongoing exposure first, revoke a credential, isolate a system, before fully understanding it. Assess, determine what data was involved and how serious the impact is, this depends entirely on the audit trail and classification labels already being in place. Notify, inform the parties who need to know, on the applicable timeline. Remediate and review, fix the underlying cause and document what the incident revealed.

Containment deliberately comes before full assessment, waiting until you know everything lets the exposure continue. A real response pulls in roles that rarely work together day to day, security for technical containment, legal for notification obligations, a privacy officer for regulatory requirements, communications for what gets said publicly, and leadership for decisions that carry business risk. An incident response plan that was never rehearsed gets discovered to be incomplete in the middle of an actual incident.

GDPR sets out two separate notification obligations. A controller must notify the supervisory authority without undue delay, where feasible not later than seventy-two hours, unless the breach is unlikely to cause risk. Separately, if the breach is likely to cause high risk to individuals, the controller must also notify those individuals directly. Not every breach triggers both, likely risk and high risk are deliberately different bars.

The assess step is a direct payoff of this course so far, classification tells you how sensitive the data was, access logs tell you who touched it, a retention schedule tells you whether it should have still existed at all. Chapter Five is complete. Next up: Chapter Six, applied case studies that put all of this together.
